t: Where Is Starbase Louisiana? SpaceX’s Pecan Island Site, Explained
d: SpaceX’s planned launch site covers about 125,000 acres near Pecan Island in southern Vermilion Parish, roughly 27 miles from Kaplan and 30 from Abbeville as the crow flies.
b:
SpaceX’s Starbase Louisiana is planned for about 125,000 acres near Pecan Island in Vermilion Parish, according to The Center Square. SpaceX’s own job postings for the project list their location as Pecan Island, La. 
 [[map]] 
 How far is it? 
 Pecan Island is a small community in the marsh country of southern Vermilion Parish, near the Gulf. Measured in a straight line from the Pecan Island community, using OpenStreetMap’s coordinates: 
   Kaplan:  about 27 miles   Abbeville:  about 30 miles   White Lake:  about 7 miles  
 Driving distances are longer, since roads in the marsh do not run straight. The Times has not seen a published map of the site’s exact boundaries, so these distances are measured to the Pecan Island community, not to a launch pad. 
 What is next to it 
 The Vermilion Parish School District owns six parcels, about 4,000 acres, north of LA 82 near White Lake, next to the planned spaceport, Acadiana News First reported Oct. 28. The land is Section 16 school property, which cannot be sold without legislative approval but can be swapped; it would be appraised before any negotiations. 
 When it will be built 
 Construction is expected to begin in 2027, with a first launch targeted for 2029, according to The Center Square. SpaceX has begun posting jobs for the site;  the Times lists every opening here . 
 For the full timeline, the money and the open questions, see  Starbase Watch .

t: SpaceX Louisiana Jobs: The First 8 Openings Posted for Pecan Island
d: SpaceX’s own job board lists eight positions at its planned Starbase Louisiana site, all senior engineering, construction, safety and community roles. Here is every one.
b:
SpaceX has started hiring for Starbase Louisiana. As of Saturday, the company’s public job board lists eight openings located in Pecan Island, La., the first jobs tied to the planned launch site in Vermilion Parish, according to a review of the listings by The Vermilion Times. 
 All eight are senior professional roles focused on getting the site built: civil and construction engineering, construction management, safety, environmental compliance, government affairs and communications. None lists a salary. 
 Every SpaceX opening at Pecan Island 
 Listed with the date each was first posted: 
   Sr. Construction Project Manager  (Starship Infrastructure, Louisiana), Sept. 16   Civil Engineer, Land Development  (Starbase Infrastructure, Louisiana), Sept. 17   Sr. Government Affairs Manager , Oct. 6   Communications Lead, Pecan Island , Oct. 12   Sr. Construction Safety Engineer , Oct. 15   Sr. Environmental Engineer , Oct. 15   Sr. Manager, Environmental Health & Safety , Oct. 15   Principal Construction Project Engineer  (Starship Infrastructure, Louisiana), Oct. 23  
 The government affairs posting says the role will work with “internal and external stakeholders” to help ensure SpaceX has “a robust and continually growing relationship with the local community.” The environmental, health and safety manager will oversee programs “at the Starship high-rate launch site,” the listing says. 
 For comparison, the same job board lists about 450 openings at SpaceX’s existing Starbase site in Texas. 
 How many jobs are coming 
 The project is expected to create 3,000 direct jobs over the next decade, with an average annual salary of $92,600, The Center Square reported. Construction is expected to begin in 2027, with a first launch targeted for 2029. 
 Whether those jobs go to Vermilion Parish residents is an open question. The parish’s tax agreement with SpaceX describes local hiring as an aspiration rather than a requirement, Acadiana News First reported, citing the citizens’ group Vermilion United. 
 How to apply 
 SpaceX posts its openings on its careers page at spacex.com/careers, where job seekers can search by location for Pecan Island. The Times will update this list as new Louisiana positions appear. 
 Follow every development on the Times’  Starbase Watch page .

t: Starbase Louisiana: What Vermilion Parish Knows So Far
d: The jobs, the money, the timeline and the questions still open about SpaceX’s planned launch site near Pecan Island, in one place.
b:
SpaceX’s Starbase Louisiana is the biggest thing to happen to Vermilion Parish in generations, and most of what residents know about it has come in pieces. Here is what has been reported, where it came from, and what is still unanswered. 
 What is planned 
 SpaceX plans what the company says will become the world’s largest spaceport on about 125,000 acres near Pecan Island, according to The Center Square. The project is expected to create 3,000 direct jobs over the next decade, with an average annual salary of $92,600. Construction is expected to begin in 2027, with a first launch targeted for 2029, the outlet reported. 
 The money 
 The parish’s payment-in-lieu-of-taxes agreement calls for SpaceX to pay the parish $25 million a year to start, rising 2% a year for 25 years, about $800 million in all by the Gulf States Newsroom’s calculation, WWNO reported. In return, the property tax exemption is worth nearly $23.8 billion over those 25 years, according to the newsroom. The Center Square estimates the full state and local incentive package at about $27.5 billion, including roughly $24 billion in property tax exemptions. 
 How it was approved 
 The parish Industrial Development Board approved the agreement on Aug. 25. That meeting’s agenda listed the deal under the code name “Project Osprey,” WWNO reported. The Police Jury had revived the board at its July 15 meeting by amending its agenda during the meeting, according to a lawsuit filed Oct. 26 by the Vermilion Citizens Coalition and three residents. The suit claims eight violations of Louisiana’s Open Meetings Law and asks a judge to void the board’s Aug. 25 approval.  The Times reported on that suit Friday.  
 What residents are asking 
 Vermilion United, a citizens’ coalition, says the agreement describes local hiring as an aspiration rather than a requirement, so the jobs are not guaranteed to parish residents, Acadiana News First reported. The group also wants a verbal SpaceX promise to supply fire equipment, meant to protect homeowners’ insurance rates, put in writing, and has asked why the development board’s administrative fee, capped at $600,000 a year, would go to a private regional group.  More on those questions here.  
 School land next door 
 The parish school district owns six parcels, about 4,000 acres of Section 16 school land, north of LA 82 near White Lake, next to the planned site, Acadiana News First reported Oct. 28. The land cannot be sold without legislative approval but can be swapped, and it would be appraised before any negotiations. 
 What comes next 
  The open meetings lawsuit is pending in the 15th Judicial District Court. No hearing date had been reported.  Louisiana Economic Development told Vermilion United the state’s cooperative endeavor agreement with SpaceX would not be released before Dec. 14, according to the group.  Kyle Ruckert, Gov. Jeff Landry’s former chief of staff, has registered as a SpaceX lobbyist, The Center Square reported.  
 The Times keeps a running timeline, the key numbers and the open questions on its  Starbase Watch page .

t: Citizen Group Presses for Answers on SpaceX Deal; Ex-Landry Aide Now a SpaceX Lobbyist
d: Vermilion United says the Starbase Louisiana tax agreement treats local hiring as a goal, not a promise, and wants a verbal SpaceX pledge on fire protection put in writing.
b:
A Vermilion Parish citizens’ coalition is raising new questions about what the Starbase Louisiana agreement actually requires of SpaceX, from local jobs to fire protection, Acadiana News First reported Thursday. 
 Vermilion United formed days after Gov. Jeff Landry announced the SpaceX deal, organizer Melissa Hargrave told the station. In less than a month, the group obtained recordings of the parish Industrial Development Board’s July 23 and Aug. 25 meetings and now posts transcripts on its website alongside the text of the signed payment-in-lieu-of-taxes, or PILOT, agreement. 
 “Our goal as a coalition is to make sure that we get as much information as possible so we can inform the public,” Hargrave said, according to the report. 
 Jobs a goal, not a guarantee 
 The group says the agreement includes employment targets but describes local hiring as an aspiration rather than a requirement, meaning it does not guarantee the jobs will go to Vermilion Parish residents, the station reported. 
 Hargrave also questioned a plan to send the Industrial Development Board’s annual administrative fee, capped at $600,000, to One Acadiana, a private regional economic development group, instead of using it to revive the parish’s own economic development district. The documents the station reviewed did not show whether that arrangement was approved. One Acadiana was unavailable for an interview before airtime, the station said. 
 Fire protection, in writing 
 The meeting recordings also touch on how a drop in the parish’s fire protection rating could raise homeowners’ insurance costs. According to the board’s lawyer, SpaceX made a verbal commitment to provide equipment if that happened. Hargrave said such a promise “needs to be codified in writing.” 
 That commitment does not appear in the signed PILOT agreement, the station reported. It could be addressed in a separate cooperative endeavor agreement between the state and SpaceX, which is not public. Hargrave said the group requested that document from Louisiana Economic Development and was told it would be at least Dec. 14 before it is released. 
 A familiar name lobbying for SpaceX 
 Separately, Kyle Ruckert, who served as Landry’s chief of staff until February, has registered as a lobbyist for SpaceX, The Center Square reported. His pay category is listed as $100,000 to $249,000. Ruckert now chairs Protect Louisiana Values, a nonprofit closely aligned with the governor, and could not be reached for comment, the outlet said. 
 According to The Center Square, the project is expected to create 3,000 direct jobs over the next decade, with construction expected to begin in 2027 and a first launch targeted for 2029. State officials negotiated an incentive package the outlet estimates at $27.5 billion, including roughly $24 billion in property tax exemptions over 25 years. 
 Both developments follow the lawsuit filed Oct. 26 by the Vermilion Citizens Coalition and three residents seeking to void the development board’s Aug. 25 approval of the tax agreement under Louisiana’s Open Meetings Law.  The Times reported on that suit Friday.

t: Kaplan Man Arrested on Drug and Firearm Charges After Search of Home
d: Investigators seized suspected methamphetamine, marijuana, prescription pills and two guns with an estimated street value of more than $68,000, KLFY reported.
b:
A 43-year-old Kaplan man has been arrested on multiple drug and firearm charges after investigators searched a home on West Second Street, KLFY reported Thursday, citing police. 
 Police said they received multiple complaints of suspected drug activity at the residence. Investigators conducted surveillance and covert operations before getting a search warrant for the home, according to the report. 
 During the search, agents seized about 308 grams of suspected methamphetamine, 171 grams of marijuana, 40 grams of synthetic marijuana and 17 Suboxone strips, KLFY reported. They also recovered 170 cyclobenzaprine tablets, 11 clonazepam tablets, half of a Xanax tablet, 11 Adderall tablets, drug paraphernalia and two firearms. 
 Authorities estimated the street value of the suspected narcotics at $68,055. No bond had been set at the time of the release, and the investigation remains ongoing, according to the report. 
 Charges are accusations, not convictions, and everyone arrested is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court. The Times does not name people arrested unless the arresting agency has released the name and charges directly; KLFY’s report did not identify the agency.

t: Residents Sue to Void Parish’s SpaceX Tax Deal Over Open Meetings Law
d: A new citizens group and three residents say the Police Jury and a revived development board broke Louisiana’s Open Meetings Law eight times while approving the Starbase Louisiana agreement.
b:
A new nonprofit and three Vermilion Parish residents have sued the Vermilion Parish Police Jury and the parish Industrial Development Board, asking a judge to void the board’s approval of the tax agreement behind SpaceX’s planned Starbase Louisiana launch site at Pecan Island. 
 The suit was filed Monday, Oct. 26, in the 15th Judicial District Court, according to WWNO and the Gulf States Newsroom. The plaintiffs are the Vermilion Citizens Coalition and residents Dr. Robert J. Young III, Rebecca C. Young and Cheryl Choate, who lives on Pecan Island. 
 What the suit alleges 
 The petition claims eight violations of Louisiana’s Open Meetings Law. Among those described in the reporting: 
  the Police Jury did not livestream its July 15 and Aug. 19 meetings;  notice of the development board’s July 23 and Aug. 25 meetings was not sent to the state commissioner of administration, and notice was posted only on the courthouse door, not online;  the Aug. 25 agenda used a code name, “Project Osprey,” instead of describing the deal;  the Police Jury amended its July 15 agenda during the meeting to revive the development board, a move the plaintiffs call a “subterfuge.”  
 The suit asks the court to void the board’s Aug. 25 actions, which approved a payment-in-lieu-of-taxes agreement with SpaceX, so the decisions would have to be made again in public. 
 The deal at stake 
 Under the agreement, SpaceX would make annual payments to the parish starting at $25 million and rising 2% a year for 25 years, roughly $800 million in all by the Gulf States Newsroom’s calculation. The newsroom reported that the property tax exemption is worth nearly $23.8 billion over the same period. 
 The plaintiffs’ attorney, William Most of New Orleans, said the Open Meetings Law is meant to “make sure that our public officials are working for us, not the other way around,” according to WWNO. 
 The Police Jury declined to comment, and the Industrial Development Board did not respond, WWNO reported. The board’s minutes say the Aug. 25 meeting notice was “duly posted and given in the manner provided by the Open Meetings Law.” The governor’s office said its executive counsel attended the July 15 meeting and that the settlement was discussed in executive session before a public vote. SpaceX did not respond to the newsroom. 
 No hearing date had been reported as of Friday. 
 School land near the site 
 Separately, the Vermilion Parish School District owns six parcels totaling about 4,000 acres north of LA 82 near White Lake, next to the planned spaceport, Acadiana News First reported Oct. 28. The land is Section 16 property, set aside by the state for public education. Parishes cannot sell Section 16 land without legislative approval but can swap it, and the report said the land would be appraised before any negotiations. 
 “Basically, we have to look at that land,” Superintendent Tommy Byler said, according to the station. No values or timeline were reported. 
 The Times will follow both stories.

t: What’s on the Ballot in Vermilion Parish on Tuesday
d: Contested races for district attorney, mayor of Erath and Gueydan, two School Board seats and more are on the Nov. 3 ballot, along with 10 statewide constitutional amendments.
b:
Vermilion Parish voters go to the polls Tuesday, Nov. 3, to choose a U.S. senator and congressman, a district attorney, two mayors, two School Board members and a long list of local officers, according to the Louisiana Secretary of State’s candidate list for the parish. Ten proposed amendments to the state constitution are also on every ballot. 
 Many local offices drew only one candidate when qualifying closed in August, and those candidates are elected without appearing on the ballot. The contested races are below. 
 Federal races 
 For  U.S. Senate , “Jamie” Davis, a Democrat, faces Julia Letlow, a Republican. 
 Six candidates are running for  U.S. Representative, 3rd Congressional District : “Kate” Cotten (Republican), John Day (Democrat), Priscilla Gonzalez (Democrat), “Clay” Higgins (Republican), Tia LeBrun (No Party) and Caleb “With a C” Walker (Democrat). 
 District attorney and courts 
 Two Republicans are running for  district attorney of the 15th Judicial District , which includes Vermilion Parish: Kristian Earles and Donald “Don” Landry. 
 In Kaplan, William J. Seaux and Ruby Thibeaux, both Republicans, are running for  Kaplan City Marshal . 
 Five court races drew a single candidate: “Tommy” Frederick and Laurie Hulin for 15th Judicial District Court judge (Divisions C and G), Richard Putnam III for Abbeville city judge, Stanton Hardee III for Kaplan city judge and Jeremiah Bolden for Abbeville city marshal. 
 School Board 
 Two of the nine School Board seats are contested: 
   District C:  Harry “Gregg” Meaux (No Party) and Coeyn Wise (No Party).   District F:  Tyrone Alexander (Democrat) and Roderick Darby (No Party).  
 Unopposed candidates in the other seven districts are David Dupuis (A), Kevin Meyers (B), “Dale” Stelly (D), Charlotte C. Detraz (E), Jason Roy (G), “Chris” Hebert (H) and “Nick” Touchet (I). 
 Towns and city 
   Mayor of Erath:  Stephanie P. Broussard (No Party) and Marlene Menard (Republican).   Mayor of Gueydan:  Jeffrey Lamson (No Party), Efrem “Zim” Livingston (Democrat) and Jason Suire (Republican).   Erath chief of police:  Anna Lapointe (No Party) and Randall Toups (Republican).   Maurice chief of police:  John Dayries and Guy Nerren, both Republicans.   Gueydan aldermen:  seven candidates for five seats.   Maurice aldermen:  six candidates for five seats.   Abbeville City Council, District A:  Cornelius Darby (Democrat) and William “Billy” Noegel (No Party).  
 Neil Arsement, the only candidate for mayor of Maurice, and Cru Delcambre, the only candidate for Gueydan police chief, were unopposed, and five candidates qualified for Erath’s five aldermen seats. 
 Justice of the peace 
 In Ward 4, Philip DeBaillon and Cheryl Granger, both Republicans, are running for  justice of the peace . Candidates for justice of the peace and constable in the parish’s other wards were unopposed. 
 Ten constitutional amendments 
 Statewide, voters will decide 10 proposed constitutional amendments. According to the ballot language published by the Secretary of State, they include: 
  letting the surviving spouse of a veteran with a service-connected disability keep a property tax exemption (Amendment 1);  barring post-conviction bail for a defendant convicted of an aggravated offense against a minor child (Amendment 3);  barring anyone who has served more than one and one-half terms as governor from being elected governor again (Amendment 4);  prohibiting expropriation of property by a foreign adversary (Amendment 8).  
 The full text of all 10 is on the Secretary of State’s website. 
 Before you go 
 Voters can look up their polling place, hours and a sample ballot on the Secretary of State’s Voter Portal at voterportal.sos.la.gov or in the GeauxVote mobile app. 
 The Vermilion Parish Police Jury office will be closed Monday, Nov. 2, for All Saints Day and Tuesday, Nov. 3, for Election Day, according to a notice on the Police Jury’s website. 
 The Times will report Vermilion Parish results after the polls
